topics.topic: Phase 3 endpoint validation precedence and classification of opposite-direction ports
questions: For one edge with multiple endpoint defects, which endpoint check and reason is the first failure, and does an opposite-direction port count as an existing port with the wrong direction or as no eligible port?

quotes:
A proof checks one flow version in this order of phases, and within a phase in
   the order named; the first check that fails is the result, with its phase, its
   node or edge and its reason:

edges, by (`to_node`, `to_port`, `from_node`, `from_port`): both ports exist
      with the right direction — the source an output of a node or an input of the
      flow, the target an input of a node or an output of the flow; both carry the same schema, the same carriage and,
      for files, the same media type (K-06) — cardinality is phase 5's; a flow
      input or output is `value` carriage;

Within one item, the conditions are checked in the order the phase
   lists them, and the first that fails is the reason.

a check naming several conditions in one sentence takes them in the
   order written; a check that fails at several items names the first in its own
   order, or, when the items have none, the smallest identifier by code point
   (A05 rule 2); a list's elements in list order.
judgement.divergence: One implementer resolves and validates the source endpoint before the target and reports that N.p has the wrong direction; another resolves the existence of both endpoints before checking either direction and reports that M.q is missing. The composing agent observes a different first proof-failure reason.
judgement.why: The text orders edges and broad phase-3 conditions but does not decompose the combined endpoint condition into an order for source existence, source direction, target existence and target direction, nor define whether an opposite-direction name satisfies existence.

witness.initial: Existing contract versions define function node N with an input port p but no output port p, and function node M with no port q; an agent has a flow version whose sole edge names N.p as its source and M.q as its target.
events: An agent composes the flow version with that edge.
The kernel proves the kept version and reaches phase 3 for the edge.
outcomes: The proof reports N.p as an existing port with the wrong direction because the source endpoint is validated completely before the target.
The proof reports M.q as missing because existence of both named endpoints is checked before the direction of N.p.
basis: | compose and prove a flow | agent | the flow version and its proof result — proven, or the first failing edge or node (State 2, A05); the version is kept either way, and the first version of a new flow name creates the flow | an unproven version cannot be activated or run |

Composition keeps any other flow version
   whether or not it is proven.
